rationale: The assistant landed on the right direction (battery most probable, confirm with Dyson support before buying) and made no unsafe or fabricated statements. However, it repeated the same 'battery protection has cut in because the voltage is too low' explanation three times, message three asked nothing and said 'we need to rule out a charger issue first' after the customer had already reported the charger light on at two sockets, and it then proposed a swap-test the customer could not do. It never asked the key confirming question about declining runtime, nor about age or warranty, so the diagnosis rested on less evidence than was available.
